title: Epoched metadata garbage collector and batcher heartbeat unification
creator: Priya Nair
description: Refactor the KV metadata lifecycle by introducing an epoched metadata garbage collector (EMGC) and consolidate multiple batcher/scheduler heartbeats into a unified, low-drift heartbeat path. Goals: reduce KV metadata memory growth under long-lived sessions, eliminate pauses caused by global GC sweeps, and remove redundant scheduler/tick timers that cause lock contention on the batcher control plane. This is a focused tech-debt effort to simplify the lifecycle code, enable fine-grained time-bounded sweeps, and reduce tail latency for multi-tenant inference workloads.
implementation_notes: 1) Introduce a per-shard epoch counter embedded in metadata headers; writers advance epoch on structural changes. 2) EMGC performs incremental, non-blocking sweep anchored to epoch checkpoints instead of global all-keys scans. 3) Replace the three existing heartbeat timers (slot-allocator, prefetch, batch-commit) with a unified heartbeat orchestrator that issues soft-notify events and shard-level tokens. 4) Add metric kv_meta_epoch_lag and kv_meta_sweep_duration_ms and tie EMGC aggressiveness to observed heap growth and tail latency. 5) Ensure forward-compatible metadata flags so older workers can participate during a rolling rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
- No global stop-the-world GC for KV metadata; sweeps are bounded to max 50ms per shard under baseline load.
- P99 generation latency reduced by >= 10% under 95th percentile concurrent sessions in canary (internal load test).
- Memory usage for idle long-lived sessions reduced by >= 20% after full sweep.
- Unified heartbeat reduces scheduler lock contention metrics (scheduler_lock_hold_ms p95) by >= 30%.
- Feature toggle (emgc_unified_heartbeat) to disable at runtime with immediate fallback path.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: rolling upgrade where older processes emit legacy metadata shape causing incorrect retention. Mitigation: add versioned metadata flag and conservative retention semantics for unknown versions; run canary for 72 hours.
Risk: EMGC may increase IO on sustained high-cardinality workloads. Mitigation: backpressure EMGC with adaptive windowing and observe eviction_throughput.
Risk: unified heartbeat could regress slot prewarming. Mitigation: synthetic prewarm scenario and preserve prewarm fast-path when heartbeat disabled.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged implementation behind emgc_unified_heartbeat.
2) Internal canary with 5% fleet for 72h (compare p50/p95/p99, kv_meta_wset_size, scheduler_lock_hold_ms).
3) Gradual ramp to 25% / 50% / 100% over 4 days if no regressions.
4) Monitor alerts: kv_meta_sweep_errors > 0, p99_gen_latency increase > 8% for 30m, memory_pressure_node_count > 1.
5) If issue, flip feature flag and rollback within 15 minutes.
observability_playbook: Primary metrics: kv_meta_sweep_duration_ms, kv_meta_epoch_lag, kv_meta_live_objects, scheduler_lock_hold_ms_p95, batcher_inflight_sessions, generation_latency_p99. Logs: EMGC shard sweep trace (trace_id), heartbeat_coalesce_events. Dashboards: runtime-refactor/emgc-heartbeat-canary. Pager: on-call infra if p99_gen_latency spike > 15% and kv_meta_sweep_errors > 0.
